resources.string: This broad outer extension of the scapular spine forms the bony tip of the shoulder and meets the clavicle.
This narrow hollow above the scapular spine is where the supraspinatus muscle begins.
This raised ridge crosses the back of the blade, separating the two hollows and widening into the acromion.
This shallow socket at the outer corner meets the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint.
This broad hollow below the scapular spine is where the infraspinatus muscle begins.
The lowest point of the shoulder blade is where its inner and outer borders meet.
The rounded upper end faces inward and meets the glenoid cavity of the scapula.
This bump lies on the outer side of the upper humerus. Three rotator cuff tendons attach here.
The deltoid muscle attaches to this rough patch on the outer side of the shaft.
This long central portion connects the rounded shoulder end to the widened elbow end.
This round joint surface on the outer side of the lower humerus meets the head of the radius.
This pulley-shaped surface lies on the inner side of the lower humerus and meets the ulna.
This is the outer half of the widened upper tibia. Its top surface meets the outer condyle of the femur at the knee.
This is the inner half of the widened upper tibia. Its top surface meets the inner condyle of the femur at the knee.
The patellar ligament attaches to this raised area on the front of the upper tibia, below the knee.
This ridge runs down from the tibial tuberosity and forms the front edge of the shin.
This shallow groove on the outer side of the lower tibia receives the lower end of the fibula.
This downward projection forms the inner ankle bump. Its inner joint surface meets the talus.
